question: Design an integration testing strategy for a Spring Boot REST API that uses PostgreSQL. How do you handle database state between tests?

keyPoints: Integration tests verify multiple components work together (controller + service + repository + database)
Use @SpringBootTest for full application context, @WebMvcTest for controller layer only
TestContainers provides real database instance in Docker, better than H2 for testing
Database cleanup strategies: @Transactional with rollback, @DirtiesContext, manual cleanup in @AfterEach
Test data builders or fixtures for consistent test setup
expectedAnswer.explanation: Integration tests validate end-to-end flows through multiple layers. Use TestContainers to spin up real PostgreSQL in Docker - this catches database-specific issues H2 misses. For test isolation: (1) @Transactional with rollback is fast but may hide transaction issues. (2) Delete all data in @AfterEach is reliable. (3) @DirtiesContext recreates context but is slow. Use test data builders for maintainable test setup. @SpringBootTest loads full context; use @WebMvcTest for controller-only tests with mocked services for faster execution.
